verified_claims: The 1m composite DTM is a raster terrain model covering approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM removes surface objects from the DSM using algorithms and manual editing.
Composite products combine Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest best-resolution source is selected.
Resampled source data is merged using bilinear interpolation.
The 1m and 2m composite datasets are supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km OS National Grid tiles.
Values are in metres and referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15 for the cited composite release.
Individual surveys contributing to the composite report vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
Coverage metadata catalogues identify the source survey used at a location.
Time Stamped DTM tiles can have 25cm, 50cm, 1m or 2m resolution depending on the survey.
Time Stamped data transformation and geoidal model can vary by survey date and must be read from metadata.
DSM includes vegetation, buildings, vehicles and terrain; DTM is the bare-earth product required for ground elevation.
WMS is for visualisation while WCS is the service intended to return elevation coverage values.
Candidate-specific measurement requires exact TQ2892 coverage, survey metadata, pixel position, NoData handling and numeric readback.
